chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al- al-Asimi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Mawali came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'We complain to you about these Arabs. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to give us gifts alongside them with equality, and he married Salman, Bilal, and Suhayb. But these [Arabs] refused us and said: We will not do it.'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) went to them and spoke to them about this. The Bedouins shouted: 'We refuse that, O Abu al-Hasan! We refuse that.' So he went out, angry, his cloak dragging behind him, saying: 'O group of Mawali! These people have reduced you to the status of the Jews and Christians. They marry their daughters to you, but do not marry their daughters to you, and they do not give you what they take. So engage in trade! May Allah bless you. For I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: Sustenance is ten parts; nine parts are in trade, and one part is in other things.'

key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: Mawali (non-Arab converts to Islam, often of Persian origin)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali advise the Mawali to do regarding economic independence and sustenance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the socio-political tension between the Mawali (non-Arab converts) and the Arab nobility during the early Islamic period, where the latter resisted full social integration despite the Prophet’s precedent. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) responded by encouraging economic self-reliance through trade, citing the Prophetic maxim that sustenance is primarily found in commerce, thereby offering a practical solution to their marginalization.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Asamy, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurra, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The partisans came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘We complain to you<sup>asws</sup> of these Arabs. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would give us the gifts along with them with the equality, and he<sup>saww</sup> got Salman<sup>as</sup>, and Bilal, and Suhayb married, and they are refusing upon us, and they are saying, We will not do it’.

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went to them and he<sup>asws</sup> spoke among them. So the Bedouins shouted, ‘We refuse that, O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>! We refuse that’. So he<sup>asws</sup> went out and he<sup>asws</sup> was angered with his<sup>asws</sup> cloak dragging, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘O group of partisans! They have considered you at the status of the Jews and the Christians. They are getting married to you (your daughters), but they are not marrying (their daughters) to you, and they are not giving you the like of what they are taking. Therefore, do business! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Bless for you, for I<sup>asws</sup> have heard Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘The sustenance is of ten parts. Nine parts are in the business and one is in something else’.
en.sarwar: 58. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Tamimiy from Ali ibn Asbat from a man who has said the following:

“I once mentioned Egypt to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You can seek to earn sustenance from it but you must not seek to stay there.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Egypt is harsh; young ones break down there.’”
